response.reason: The closed FCSTM shows InMotion's substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) are structurally present and contain the required transitions/actions, but the InMotion composite's own initial pseudostate edge targets a compiler-synthesized UnspecifiedInitial state rather than Accelerating, making the entire Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching subgraph and all of its outgoing event consumers unreachable from root. This drives a cluster of behavioral-consequence defects: the NL5 owner-scoped initial_entry contract is violated because InMotion's initial edge does not reach Accelerating; and every event_consumption contract whose consumer states live inside InMotion's substates (Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate x2) is unconsumed in practice because inspection-equivalent/verify facts explicitly mark those consumer transitions as unreachable, even though the edges exist structurally (transition_fact only proves declaration, not operational coverage). Closed/SendDeparted and Arrived/Stop,Send Arrived consumers remain reachable per the deterministic facts, so those two event_consumption contracts and the associated endpoint contracts for DoorsClosing->InMotion and InMotion->Stopping/EmergencyStopping are satisfied and omitted. Because Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching are unreachable, I add one derived reachability contract capturing that these three author-grounded operating states (jointly the whole InMotion substate machine) must be reachable from root/InMotion, consistent with NL4/NL5's requirement that the system actually operates through these substates as part of the train's motion behavior. The containment, cardinality, and satisfied endpoint/action contracts among these substates are not re-flagged as separate issues since the causal root cause is the isolated initial-entry defect, per frontier discipline to keep one candidate per distinct property.

cardinality_bindings.basis: NL-CONTRACT-NL4-CARD-1 quote 'the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'; exact_source_inventory.states rows for InMotion.Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching all list parent=InMotion; fcstm_model.model_ir owned closed_model_inventory shows InMotion composite owning Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching, and UnspecifiedInitial as direct children.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 directly counts three named child substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) owned by the InMotion composite; this is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation. The InMotion composite has no stated concurrent/orthogonal region structure, so concurrent_regions is not the primary reading; a non-empty composite without a separator constitutes one implicit region, which is not the counted domain here. output.reason: The closed FCSTM shows InMotion's substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) are structurally present and contain the required transitions/actions, but the InMotion composite's own initial pseudostate edge targets a compiler-synthesized UnspecifiedInitial state rather than Accelerating, making the entire Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching subgraph and all of its outgoing event consumers unreachable from root. This drives a cluster of behavioral-consequence defects: the NL5 owner-scoped initial_entry contract is violated because InMotion's initial edge does not reach Accelerating; and every event_consumption contract whose consumer states live inside InMotion's substates (Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate x2) is unconsumed in practice because inspection-equivalent/verify facts explicitly mark those consumer transitions as unreachable, even though the edges exist structurally (transition_fact only proves declaration, not operational coverage). Closed/SendDeparted and Arrived/Stop,Send Arrived consumers remain reachable per the deterministic facts, so those two event_consumption contracts and the associated endpoint contracts for DoorsClosing->InMotion and InMotion->Stopping/EmergencyStopping are satisfied and omitted. Because Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching are unreachable, I add one derived reachability contract capturing that these three author-grounded operating states (jointly the whole InMotion substate machine) must be reachable from root/InMotion, consistent with NL4/NL5's requirement that the system actually operates through these substates as part of the train's motion behavior. The containment, cardinality, and satisfied endpoint/action contracts among these substates are not re-flagged as separate issues since the causal root cause is the isolated initial-entry defect, per frontier discipline to keep one candidate per distinct property.

candidates.reason: G1 finite path-existence/unreachable-target semantics directly express the deterministic refuted reachability facts for these three states from the closed model's initial entry; this is the minimal frozen predicate deciding the reachability property distinct from the narrower initial_entry contract.
candidates.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: This global reachability defect and the InMotion->Accelerating initial-entry defect (NL5) may be viewed as the same root cause expressed at two granularities; a reviewer could argue only one contract is needed. However, NL4 independently states an operating obligation over all three substates as motion phases, which is a broader and distinct claim from the single owner-local edge property, justifying a separate reachability contract per frontier discipline for narrowest global reachability scope.
candidates.title: InMotion's authored operating substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) are globally unreachable from root

cardinality_bindings.basis: NL-CONTRACT-NL4-CARD-1 quote 'the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'; exact_source_inventory.states rows for InMotion.Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching all list parent=InMotion; fcstm_model.model_ir owned closed_model_inventory shows InMotion composite owning Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching, and UnspecifiedInitial as direct children.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 directly counts three named child substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) owned by the InMotion composite; this is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation. The InMotion composite has no stated concurrent/orthogonal region structure, so concurrent_regions is not the primary reading; a non-empty composite without a separator constitutes one implicit region, which is not the counted domain here. The owner binds to the contract-level InMotion scope itself, consistent with both lenses using the same owner rule.

result.reason: The closed FCSTM shows InMotion's substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) are structurally present and contain the required transitions/actions, but the InMotion composite's own initial pseudostate edge targets a compiler-synthesized UnspecifiedInitial state rather than Accelerating, making the entire Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching subgraph and all of its outgoing event consumers unreachable from root. This drives a cluster of behavioral-consequence defects: the NL5 owner-scoped initial_entry contract is violated because InMotion's initial edge does not reach Accelerating; and every event_consumption contract whose consumer states live inside InMotion's substates (Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate x2) is unconsumed in practice because inspection-equivalent/verify facts explicitly mark those consumer transitions as unreachable, even though the edges exist structurally (transition_fact only proves declaration, not operational coverage). Closed/SendDeparted and Arrived/Stop,Send Arrived consumers remain reachable per the deterministic facts, so those two event_consumption contracts and the associated endpoint contracts for DoorsClosing->InMotion and InMotion->Stopping/EmergencyStopping are satisfied and omitted. Because Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching are unreachable, I add one derived reachability contract capturing that these three author-grounded operating states (jointly the whole InMotion substate machine) must be reachable from root/InMotion, consistent with NL4/NL5's requirement that the system actually operates through these substates as part of the train's motion behavior. The containment, cardinality, and satisfied endpoint/action contracts among these substates are not re-flagged as separate issues since the causal root cause is the isolated initial-entry defect, per frontier discipline to keep one candidate per distinct property.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 9-18; inspection_equivalent_facts.states; verify_facts.checks initial-entry:transition:line:18; S2 receipt verdict=false.
decisions.reason: The closed FCSTM model's InMotion scope contains '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;' (transition:line:18), and the S2 backend receipt confirms verdict=false for the exact InMotion.[*]->Accelerating edge. NL5 states 'The system begins in the Accelerating substate', requiring an owner-local default-entry edge into Accelerating; the exact model instead routes to a distinct synthetic placeholder state with no further path into Accelerating (per inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_from_initial=false for Accelerating). This establishes the missing owner-local edge. The strongest alternative reading is that UnspecifiedInitial is a compiler-synthesized artifact standing in for an unauthored default-entry choice, and that a human reviewer might treat this as the same underlying defect as the sibling dossiers (i1, i6) at a different element-set granularity rather than a wholly independent fault; this is a competent but non-dispositive alternative reading of scope/counting, not a rebuttal, since the exact edge to Accelerating is still absent in every reading.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL5 requires InMotion's owner-local initial pseudostate edge to enter Accelerating specifically.

decisions.basis: canonical_source_ir/plantuml_source line 8; fcstm_model transition:line:18; inspection_equivalent_facts.states; S2 receipt verdict=false.
decisions.reason: Author-source PlantUML (line 8 region) never authored an explicit '[*] -> Accelerating' edge inside InMotion; the compiler synthesized UnspecifiedInitial to fill the gap, and the closed model shows this synthetic state has no continuation into Accelerating (S2 verdict=false; Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching reachable_from_initial=false). NL5 nonetheless requires functional entry into Accelerating as the system's starting substate, which is unmet. The plausible alternative is that the missing explicit source syntax, rather than a modeling defect proper, is the origin of UnspecifiedInitial, and this obligation substantially overlaps with i0/i6 at the same owner/target pair; that is a competent scope/attribution reading but does not establish that Accelerating is actually entered, so grounding remains established with the defect surviving as an undercutting alternative characterization rather than a rebuttal.
decisions.violated_obligation: InMotion must own an initial pseudostate edge ([*] -> Accelerating) reaching Accelerating as its default entry.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row Reached_Cruising_Cruise; verify_facts.checks refuted; fcstm_model transition:line:19.

This is exactly the reachable-consumer coverage violation the property protocol calls out: a declared consumer transition does not rebut a requirement for a reachable consumer. The proposed rebuttal -- that this is purely a downstream consequence of the InMotion initial-entry fault rather than an independent defect -- is contradicted by the property-preservation rule that unreachability is a distinct, separately assessed property from the wrong-endpoint/initial-entry defect; the exact deterministic fact (empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs) stands on its own and is not defeated by attributing its cause elsewhere. No unsupported-predicate excuse applies since this is a coverage-fact reading, not backend unavailability alone.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Reached_Cruising_Cruise event's consumer transition (Accelerating->Cruising) must be reachable and consumable during an actual run.

issues.expected: The three authored operating substates that NL4/NL5 require the train to actually pass through must be reachable from the root/InMotion entry.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.states marks Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching as reachable_from_initial=false; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics reports STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for all three; verify_facts.checks.non_proved confirms refuted reachability for each; the InMotion scope's only default entry routes to the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state, which itself only leads to termination effects, never into the substate chain.
issues.reason: G1 finite path-existence/unreachable-target semantics directly express the deterministic refuted reachability facts for these three states from the closed model's initial entry; this is the minimal frozen predicate deciding the reachability property distinct from the narrower initial_entry contract.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: This global reachability defect and the InMotion->Accelerating initial-entry defect (NL5) may be viewed as the same root cause expressed at two granularities; a reviewer could argue only one contract is needed. However, NL4 independently states an operating obligation over all three substates as motion phases, which is a broader and distinct claim from the single owner-local edge property, justifying a separate reachability contract per frontier discipline for narrowest global reachability scope.

cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 directly counts three named child substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) owned by the InMotion composite; this is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation. The InMotion composite has no stated concurrent/orthogonal region structure, so concurrent_regions is not the primary reading; a non-empty composite without a separator constitutes one implicit region, which is not the counted domain here. The owner binds to the contract-level InMotion scope itself, consistent with both lenses using the same owner rule.

branches.reason: The closed FCSTM shows InMotion's substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) are structurally present and contain the required transitions/actions, but the InMotion composite's own initial pseudostate edge targets a compiler-synthesized UnspecifiedInitial state rather than Accelerating, making the entire Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching subgraph and all of its outgoing event consumers unreachable from root. This drives a cluster of behavioral-consequence defects: the NL5 owner-scoped initial_entry contract is violated because InMotion's initial edge does not reach Accelerating; and every event_consumption contract whose consumer states live inside InMotion's substates (Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate x2) is unconsumed in practice because inspection-equivalent/verify facts explicitly mark those consumer transitions as unreachable, even though the edges exist structurally (transition_fact only proves declaration, not operational coverage).
